schema.hook_field: applies_to: all type: string (enum) required: true default: none applicability: cli excerpt: | "command", "http", "prompt", or "agent" source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "Common fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

applies_to: all type: string (permission rule syntax) required: false default: none (runs on all matches) applicability: cli excerpt: | Permission rule syntax to filter when this hook runs, such as "Bash(git *)" or "Edit(*.ts)". The hook only spawns if the tool call matches the pattern. Only evaluated on tool events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, and PermissionDenied. On other events, a hook with `if` set never runs. Uses the same syntax as permission rules. caveats: - "Only evaluated on tool events. On non-tool events, a hook with `if` set never runs." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "Common fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

applies_to: all type: number (seconds) required: false default: "600 for command, 30 for prompt, 60 for agent" applicability: cli excerpt: | Seconds before canceling. Defaults: 600 for command, 30 for prompt, 60 for agent source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "Common fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

applies_to: all type: string required: false default: none applicability: cli excerpt: | Custom spinner message displayed while the hook runs source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "Common fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

applies_to: all type: boolean required: false default: false applicability: cli excerpt: | If true, runs only once per session then is removed. Skills only, not agents. See Hooks in skills and agents. caveats: - "Skills only — not available for agent-registered hooks." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "Common fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

applies_to: command type: string required: true default: none applicability: cli excerpt: | Shell command to execute source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "Command hook fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

applies_to: command type: boolean required: false default: false applicability: cli excerpt: | If true, runs in the background without blocking. See Run hooks in the background. source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "Command hook fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

applies_to: command type: boolean required: false default: false applicability: cli excerpt: | If true, runs in the background and wakes Claude on exit code 2. Implies async. The hook's stderr, or stdout if stderr is empty, is shown to Claude as a system reminder so it can react to a long-running background failure. caveats: - "Implies async: true." - "Only exit code 2 triggers the rewake; other non-zero codes do not." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "Command hook fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

applies_to: command type: string (enum) required: false default: "bash" applicability: cli excerpt: | Shell to use for this hook. Accepts "bash" (default) or "powershell". Setting "powershell" runs the command via PowerShell on Windows. Does not require CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL since hooks spawn PowerShell directly. source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "Command hook fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

applies_to: http type: string (URL) required: true default: none applicability: cli excerpt: | URL to send the POST request to source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "HTTP hook fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

applies_to: http type: object (key-value string pairs) required: false default: none applicability: cli excerpt: | Additional HTTP headers as key-value pairs. Values support environment variable interpolation using $VAR_NAME or ${VAR_NAME} syntax. Only variables listed in allowedEnvVars are resolved. caveats: - "Only variables listed in allowedEnvVars are resolved. Other references are replaced with empty strings." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "HTTP hook fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

applies_to: http type: array of strings required: false default: none (no interpolation occurs without this field) applicability: cli excerpt: | List of environment variable names that may be interpolated into header values. References to unlisted variables are replaced with empty strings. Required for any env var interpolation to work. source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "HTTP hook fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

applies_to: prompt-agent type: string required: true default: none applicability: cli excerpt: | Prompt text to send to the model. Use $ARGUMENTS as a placeholder for the hook input JSON. source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "Prompt and agent hook fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

applies_to: prompt-agent type: string required: false default: "a fast model (unspecified)" applicability: cli excerpt: | Model to use for evaluation. Defaults to a fast model. source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "Prompt and agent hook fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00
schema.hook_io: description: | Fields sent as JSON to ALL hook handlers. For command hooks this arrives on stdin. For HTTP hooks it arrives as the POST request body. fields: session_id: description: "Current session identifier" transcript_path: description: "Path to conversation JSON" cwd: description: "Current working directory when the hook is invoked" permission_mode: description: | Current permission mode: "default", "plan", "acceptEdits", "auto", "dontAsk", or "bypassPermissions". Not all events receive this field: see each event's JSON example to check. hook_event_name: description: "Name of the event that fired" subagent_extra_fields: description: | When running with --agent or inside a subagent, two additional fields are included. agent_id: description: | Unique identifier for the subagent. Present only when the hook fires inside a subagent call. Use this to distinguish subagent hook calls from main-thread calls. agent_type: description: | Agent name (for example, "Explore" or "security-reviewer"). Present when the session uses --agent or the hook fires inside a subagent. For subagents, the subagent's type takes precedence over the session's --agent value. source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "Common input fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

description: | The exit code from a command hook tells Claude Code whether the action should proceed, be blocked, or be ignored. exit_0: meaning: "Success. Claude Code parses stdout for JSON output fields. JSON is only processed on exit 0." notes: | For most events, stdout is written to the debug log but not shown in the transcript. Exceptions: UserPromptSubmit and SessionStart, where stdout is added as context Claude can see and act on. exit_2: meaning: "Blocking error. Claude Code ignores stdout/JSON. stderr text is fed back to Claude as an error message." notes: | Effect depends on the event: PreToolUse blocks the tool call, UserPromptSubmit rejects the prompt, etc. See exit-code-2-behavior-per-event table. other_codes: meaning: "Non-blocking error for most events. Shows a hook-name hook error notice with first line of stderr. Execution continues." caveats: - "WorktreeCreate is the exception: any non-zero exit code aborts worktree creation." - "Exit code 1 is treated as non-blocking (not a blocking error), even though it is the conventional Unix failure code." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "Exit code output" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

description: | On exit 0, hooks can print a JSON object to stdout for finer-grained control. For HTTP hooks the JSON is the response body. Must use one approach per hook: exit codes alone OR exit 0 + JSON. JSON is only processed on exit 0. output_cap: "Hook output injected into context is capped at 10,000 characters. Excess is saved to a file and replaced with a preview and file path." universal_fields: continue: type: boolean default: "true" description: | If false, Claude stops processing entirely after the hook runs. Takes precedence over any event-specific decision fields. stopReason: type: string default: none description: "Message shown to the user when continue is false. Not shown to Claude." suppressOutput: type: boolean default: "false" description: "If true, omits stdout from the debug log." systemMessage: type: string default: none description: "Warning message shown to the user." top_level_decision_fields: decision: values: ["block"] description: | Used by UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop, SubagentStop, ConfigChange, PreCompact. "block" is the only value. Omit to allow. reason: description: "Explanation shown to Claude (or user) when decision is block." hook_specific_output: description: | A nested object for events that need richer control. Requires a hookEventName field set to the event name. Used by PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied, WorktreeCreate, Elicitation, ElicitationResult, and others. source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "JSON output" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

description: "HTTP hooks use HTTP status codes and response bodies instead of exit codes and stdout." responses: 2xx_empty_body: "Success, equivalent to exit code 0 with no output." 2xx_plain_text: "Success, the text is added as context." 2xx_json: "Success, parsed using the same JSON output schema as command hooks." non_2xx: "Non-blocking error, execution continues." connection_failure_or_timeout: "Non-blocking error, execution continues." caveats: - "HTTP hooks cannot signal a blocking error through status codes alone. To block, return 2xx with JSON containing the appropriate decision fields." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "HTTP response handling" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00
schema.matcher_spec: description: | The matcher field filters when hooks fire. How a matcher is evaluated depends on the characters it contains. evaluation_rules: - pattern: '"*", "", or omitted' evaluated_as: "Match all — fires on every occurrence of the event." - pattern: "Only letters, digits, _, and |" evaluated_as: 'Exact string, or |-separated list of exact strings. Example: "Bash" matches only Bash; "Edit|Write" matches either.' - pattern: "Contains any other character" evaluated_as: "JavaScript regular expression. Example: ^Notebook matches any tool starting with Notebook." per_event_matcher_values: - events: ["PreToolUse", "PostToolUse", "PostToolUseFailure", "PermissionRequest", "PermissionDenied"] filters: "tool name" examples: ["Bash", "Edit|Write", "mcp__.*"] - events: ["SessionStart"] filters: "how the session started" examples: ["startup", "resume", "clear", "compact"] - events: ["SessionEnd"] filters: "why the session ended" examples: ["clear", "resume", "logout", "prompt_input_exit", "bypass_permissions_disabled", "other"] - events: ["Notification"] filters: "notification type" examples: ["permission_prompt", "idle_prompt", "auth_success", "elicitation_dialog"] - events: ["SubagentStart", "SubagentStop"] filters: "agent type" examples: ["Bash", "Explore", "Plan", "custom agent names"] - events: ["PreCompact", "PostCompact"] filters: "what triggered compaction" examples: ["manual", "auto"] - events: ["ConfigChange"] filters: "configuration source" examples: ["user_settings", "project_settings", "local_settings", "policy_settings", "skills"] - events: ["StopFailure"] filters: "error type" examples: ["rate_limit", "authentication_failed", "billing_error", "invalid_request", "server_error", "max_output_tokens", "unknown"] - events: ["InstructionsLoaded"] filters: "load reason" examples: ["session_start", "nested_traversal", "path_glob_match", "include", "compact"] - events: ["Elicitation", "ElicitationResult"] filters: "MCP server name" examples: ["configured MCP server names"] - events: ["FileChanged"] filters: "literal filenames to watch (pipe-separated list — NOT regex)" examples: [".envrc|.env", "package.json"] caveats: - "FileChanged does not follow the standard matcher rules. Matcher is a pipe-separated list of literal filenames to watch in the current working directory. Matcher value is required and must be non-empty." - events: ["CwdChanged"] filters: "no matcher support — always fires on every directory change" examples: [] - events: ["UserPromptSubmit", "Stop", "TeammateIdle", "TaskCreated", "TaskCompleted", "WorktreeCreate", "WorktreeRemove"] filters: "no matcher support — always fires on every occurrence" examples: [] caveats: - "If a matcher field is added to these events, it is silently ignored." mcp_tool_naming: pattern: "mcp____" examples: - "mcp__memory__create_entities" - "mcp__filesystem__read_file" - "mcp__github__search_repositories" wildcard_note: | To match every tool from a server, append .* to the server prefix. The .* is required: a matcher like mcp__memory contains only letters and underscores, so it is compared as an exact string and matches no tool. wildcard_examples: - "mcp__memory__.* — matches all tools from the memory server" - "mcp__.*__write.* — matches any tool whose name starts with write from any server" if_field_note: | For tool events, you can filter more narrowly by setting the if field on individual hook handlers. if uses permission rule syntax to match against the tool name and arguments together, so "Bash(git *)" runs only for git commands and "Edit(*.ts)" runs only for TypeScript files. source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "Matcher patterns" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00
schema.hook_event: when: "When Claude Code starts a new session or resumes an existing session." decision_control: false matcher_values: ["startup", "resume", "clear", "compact"] supported_hook_types: ["command only"] input_shape: | Common fields plus: source: string — "startup" | "resume" | "clear" | "compact" model: string — model identifier agent_type: string (optional) — agent name if started with --agent exit_code_behavior: | Exit 2: shows stderr to user only (cannot block session start). Exit 0: stdout added as context Claude can see. output_specific_fields: | hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext: string added to Claude's context. Multiple hooks' values are concatenated. special_env: | CLAUDE_ENV_FILE is available: write export statements to persist environment variables for subsequent Bash commands in this session. caveats: - "Only type: command hooks are supported." - "Runs on every session — keep hooks fast." - "CLAUDE_ENV_FILE available for persisting env vars (use append >> to preserve other hooks' vars)." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "SessionStart" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

when: | When a CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/*.md file is loaded into context. Fires at session start for eagerly-loaded files and again later when files are lazily loaded, for example when Claude accesses a subdirectory that contains a nested CLAUDE.md or when conditional rules with paths: frontmatter match. decision_control: false matcher_values: ["session_start", "nested_traversal", "path_glob_match", "include", "compact"] input_shape: | Common fields plus: file_path: string — absolute path to the instruction file that was loaded memory_type: string — "User" | "Project" | "Local" | "Managed" load_reason: string — "session_start" | "nested_traversal" | "path_glob_match" | "include" | "compact" globs: array (optional) — path glob patterns from file's paths: frontmatter; present only for path_glob_match loads trigger_file_path: string (optional) — path to file whose access triggered this load, for lazy loads parent_file_path: string (optional) — path to parent instruction file that included this one, for include loads exit_code_behavior: | Exit code is ignored. The hook runs asynchronously for observability purposes only. caveats: - "No decision control — cannot block or modify instruction loading." - "Runs asynchronously." - "The compact load_reason fires when instruction files are re-loaded after a compaction event." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "InstructionsLoaded" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

when: "When the user submits a prompt, before Claude processes it." decision_control: true matcher_values: ["no matcher support — always fires on every occurrence"] input_shape: | Common fields plus: prompt: string — the text the user submitted exit_code_behavior: | Exit 2: blocks prompt processing and erases the prompt. stderr shown to user. Exit 0: plain text stdout added as context Claude can see. JSON output parsed for decision fields. output_specific_fields: | decision: "block" prevents the prompt from being processed and erases it from context. reason: shown to the user when decision is "block". Not added to context. hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext: string added to Claude's context (more discrete than plain stdout). hookSpecificOutput.sessionTitle: sets the session title, same effect as /rename. caveats: - "Plain stdout is shown as hook output in the transcript. additionalContext is added more discretely." - "Matcher field is silently ignored if added." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "UserPromptSubmit" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

when: "After Claude creates tool parameters and before processing the tool call." decision_control: true matcher_values: ["Bash", "Edit", "Write", "Read", "Glob", "Grep", "Agent", "WebFetch", "WebSearch", "AskUserQuestion", "ExitPlanMode", "and any MCP tool names"] input_shape: | Common fields plus: tool_name: string — name of the tool tool_input: object — tool-specific parameters (see per-tool schemas below) tool_use_id: string — unique identifier for the tool call Per-tool input shapes: Bash: { command: string, description?: string, timeout?: number, run_in_background?: boolean } Write: { file_path: string, content: string } Edit: { file_path: string, old_string: string, new_string: string, replace_all?: boolean } Read: { file_path: string, offset?: number, limit?: number } Glob: { pattern: string, path?: string } Grep: { pattern: string, path?: string, glob?: string, output_mode?: string, "-i"?: boolean, multiline?: boolean } WebFetch: { url: string, prompt: string } WebSearch: { query: string, allowed_domains?: array, blocked_domains?: array } Agent: { prompt: string, description?: string, subagent_type?: string, model?: string } AskUserQuestion: { questions: array, answers?: object } exit_code_behavior: | Exit 2: blocks the tool call. stderr fed back to Claude. Exit 0: JSON output parsed for hookSpecificOutput decision fields. output_specific_fields: | hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName: "PreToolUse" hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision: "allow" | "deny" | "ask" | "defer" allow — skips permission prompt deny — prevents the tool call (reason shown to Claude) ask — prompts the user to confirm (reason shown to user, not Claude) defer — pauses tool call for external process to resume (non-interactive mode only, requires v2.1.89+) hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecisionReason: string For allow and ask: shown to user, not Claude. For deny: shown to Claude. For defer: ignored. hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput: object — replaces entire tool input before execution hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext: string added to Claude's context before tool executes Precedence when multiple hooks return different decisions: deny > defer > ask > allow caveats: - "Top-level decision and reason fields are deprecated for this event. Use hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision and hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecisionReason." - "Deprecated values approve and block map to allow and deny respectively." - "defer only works in non-interactive mode (-p flag) and when Claude makes a single tool call. Requires v2.1.89+." - "For AskUserQuestion and ExitPlanMode: returning allow alone is not sufficient in non-interactive mode; must also supply updatedInput with answers." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "PreToolUse" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

when: "When the user is shown a permission dialog." decision_control: true matcher_values: ["tool name — same values as PreToolUse"] input_shape: | Common fields plus: tool_name: string tool_input: object — tool-specific parameters (same structure as PreToolUse, without tool_use_id) permission_suggestions: array (optional) — "always allow" options the user would normally see in the permission dialog. Each entry: { type: string, rules?: array, behavior?: string, destination?: string } exit_code_behavior: | Exit 2: denies the permission. stderr shown as blocking error. Exit 0: JSON output parsed for hookSpecificOutput decision. output_specific_fields: | hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName: "PermissionRequest" hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior: "allow" | "deny" hookSpecificOutput.decision.updatedInput: object (for allow only) — modifies tool input before execution hookSpecificOutput.decision.updatedPermissions: array (for allow only) — permission update entries to apply Entry types: addRules, replaceRules, removeRules, setMode, addDirectories, removeDirectories Each entry has a destination: session | localSettings | projectSettings | userSettings hookSpecificOutput.decision.message: string (for deny only) — tells Claude why permission was denied hookSpecificOutput.decision.interrupt: boolean (for deny only) — if true, stops Claude caveats: - "Fires when a permission dialog is about to be shown to the user. PreToolUse fires before tool execution regardless of permission status." - "tool_use_id is not present (unlike PreToolUse)." - "A hook can echo one of the permission_suggestions it received as its own updatedPermissions output." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "PermissionRequest" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

when: "Immediately after a tool completes successfully." decision_control: true matcher_values: ["tool name — same values as PreToolUse"] input_shape: | Common fields plus: tool_name: string tool_input: object — arguments sent to the tool tool_response: object — result the tool returned (schema depends on tool) tool_use_id: string exit_code_behavior: | Exit 2: shows stderr to Claude (tool already ran — cannot block retroactively). Exit 0: JSON output parsed for decision fields. output_specific_fields: | decision: "block" prompts Claude with the reason. Omit to allow. reason: explanation shown to Claude when decision is "block". hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext: additional context for Claude to consider. hookSpecificOutput.updatedMCPToolOutput: for MCP tools only — replaces the tool's output with the provided value. source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "PostToolUse" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

when: "When a tool execution fails — for tool calls that throw errors or return failure results." decision_control: false matcher_values: ["tool name — same values as PreToolUse"] input_shape: | Common fields plus: tool_name: string tool_input: object — arguments sent to the tool tool_use_id: string error: string — describes what went wrong is_interrupt: boolean (optional) — whether the failure was caused by user interruption exit_code_behavior: | Exit 2: shows stderr to Claude (tool already failed). Exit 0: JSON output parsed. output_specific_fields: | hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext: additional context for Claude to consider alongside the error. source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "PostToolUseFailure" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

when: | When the auto mode classifier denies a tool call. Only fires in auto mode. Does not run when the user manually denies a permission dialog, when a PreToolUse hook blocks a call, or when a deny rule matches. decision_control: true matcher_values: ["tool name — same values as PreToolUse"] input_shape: | Common fields plus: tool_name: string tool_input: object tool_use_id: string reason: string — the classifier's explanation for why the tool call was denied exit_code_behavior: | Exit code and stderr are ignored (denial already occurred). Use JSON hookSpecificOutput.retry: true to tell the model it may retry. output_specific_fields: | hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName: "PermissionDenied" hookSpecificOutput.retry: boolean — if true, Claude Code adds a message telling the model it may retry the tool call. The denial itself is not reversed. caveats: - "Only fires in auto mode." - "Exit code and stderr are ignored." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "PermissionDenied" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

when: "When Claude Code sends notifications." decision_control: false matcher_values: ["permission_prompt", "idle_prompt", "auth_success", "elicitation_dialog"] input_shape: | Common fields plus: message: string — notification text title: string (optional) notification_type: string — which type fired exit_code_behavior: | Exit 2: shows stderr to user only. Cannot block or modify notifications. Exit 0: JSON output parsed. output_specific_fields: | hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext: string added to Claude's context. source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "Notification" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

when: "When a Claude Code subagent is spawned via the Agent tool." decision_control: false matcher_values: ["agent type name: built-in agents like Bash, Explore, Plan, or custom agent names from .claude/agents/"] input_shape: | Common fields plus: agent_id: string — unique identifier for the subagent agent_type: string — agent name (built-in like "Bash", "Explore", "Plan", or custom) exit_code_behavior: | Exit 2: shows stderr to user only (cannot block subagent creation). Exit 0: JSON output parsed. output_specific_fields: | hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext: string added to the subagent's context. caveats: - "Cannot block subagent creation, only inject context." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "SubagentStart" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

when: "When a Claude Code subagent has finished responding." decision_control: true matcher_values: ["agent type — same values as SubagentStart"] input_shape: | Common fields plus: stop_hook_active: boolean agent_id: string agent_type: string — value used for matcher filtering agent_transcript_path: string — subagent's own transcript (stored in subagents/ folder) last_assistant_message: string — text content of the subagent's final response Note: transcript_path is the main session's transcript; agent_transcript_path is the subagent's. exit_code_behavior: | Exit 2: prevents the subagent from stopping. Same decision control format as Stop hooks. Exit 0: JSON output parsed. output_specific_fields: | Same decision control format as Stop hooks: decision: "block" prevents the subagent from stopping. reason: explanation shown to Claude when decision is "block". caveats: - "In settings files, Stop hooks are automatically converted to SubagentStop when running in a subagent context." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "SubagentStop" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

when: "When a task is being created via the TaskCreate tool." decision_control: true matcher_values: ["no matcher support — fires on every occurrence"] input_shape: | Common fields plus: task_id: string — identifier of the task being created task_subject: string — title of the task task_description: string (optional) — detailed description teammate_name: string (optional) — name of the teammate creating the task team_name: string (optional) — name of the team exit_code_behavior: | Exit 2: task is not created; stderr message is fed back to the model as feedback. Exit 0: JSON output parsed. output_specific_fields: | JSON {"continue": false, "stopReason": "..."}: stops the teammate entirely. The stopReason is shown to the user. caveats: - "Matcher field silently ignored." - "Two distinct block patterns: exit 2 (re-runs model with feedback) vs continue:false (stops teammate entirely)." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "TaskCreated" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

when: "When a task is being marked as completed via TaskComplete." decision_control: true matcher_values: ["no matcher support — fires on every occurrence"] input_shape: | Common fields plus (identical to TaskCreated input): task_id: string task_subject: string task_description: string (optional) teammate_name: string (optional) team_name: string (optional) exit_code_behavior: | Exit 2: task is not marked as completed; stderr message is fed back to the model. Exit 0: JSON output parsed. output_specific_fields: | JSON {"continue": false, "stopReason": "..."}: stops the teammate entirely. The stopReason is shown to the user. caveats: - "Matcher field silently ignored." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks section: "TaskCompleted" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T12:32:03-04:00

when: "When Claude is about to finish responding." decision_control: true matcher_values: ["no matcher support — always fires on every occurrence"] input_shape: | Common fields plus: last_assistant_message: string — text of Claude's final response exit_code_behavior: | Exit 2: prevents Claude from stopping, continues the conversation.
